en: Itivuttaka 83:
Tikanipāta, Catutthavagga (The Fourth Chapter)
The Discourse on the Five Portents.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Bhikkhus, when a deva is subject to falling away from the deva-body, five portents appear to him:..."
Their garlands wither, their clothes become soiled, sweat breaks forth from their armpits, disfigurement comes over their bodies, and the deva no longer delights in his own celestial throne.
Then, monks, the other devas, knowing "This son of the gods is subject to falling," express their approval with three words:
"Go from here, sir, to a happy destination."
“Having gone to a happy destination, may you obtain a well-gained gain.
Having obtained a well-gained gain, may you be well-established.
When this was said, a certain bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, what indeed is it that constitutes for the devas their going to a good destination?
And what, venerable sir, is it that constitutes for the devas their gain of what is well-gained?
Furthermore, venerable sir, what is it that constitutes for the devas their being well-established?”
“Human existence, bhikkhu, is reckoned by the devas as going to a happy destination.
That one, being human, gains faith in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata—
this, bhikkhu, is reckoned by the devas as a well-gotten gain.”
Moreover, that faith of his is settled, rooted, established, firm, and unshakable by any ascetic, brahmin, deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone else in the world.
This, monk, is what is reckoned as the "well-established" of the devas.
Thus the Blessed One spoke this matter.
In this regard, it is said:
“When a deva falls from the host of devas at the exhaustion of his lifespan;”
Three sounds resounded as the gods rejoiced:
“O sir, go from here to a happy destination!”
In the company of human beings,
having become a human, may you obtain supreme faith in the true Dhamma.
That faith of yours is established,
rooted, and firmly grounded;
it shall remain unshakable for as long as life lasts.
In the well-proclaimed True Dhamma,
having abandoned misconduct of body and misconduct of speech;
Having abandoned misconduct of mind and whatever else is associated with hatred,
having performed wholesome deeds with the body,
Having performed much wholesome action by speech,
and having performed wholesome action by mind that is immeasurable and free from substrate.
Then, having performed much merit pertaining to the acquisitions through giving,
[he established] other people as well in the true Dhamma.
"Establish him in the holy life.
When the wise gods, out of compassion, [address] a god in this way;
“They rejoice in his departure, saying:
‘Come again and again, O Lord!
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The fourth.
